name: Qaiyo UTM Tracker for Fluent Forms
author: qaiyo

sections.description:
You run ads on Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn or Microsoft, the enquiries arrive through Fluent Forms, and the question is always the same: which source and which campaign brought this lead? Qaiyo UTM Tracker for Fluent Forms answers it on every entry, and adds them up in a report inside Fluent Forms, with no external reporting tool in between.

Click one button to add the tracking fields to a form. From then on the plugin remembers where the visitor arrived from — the campaign parameters of the ad, or the search engine, social network or website that sent them — writes it into those fields when the form is sent, and Fluent Forms stores it with the entry: visible on the Entries screen, in exports and in Fluent Forms’ own reports.

What makes it different

  • The values live in the Fluent Forms entry itself. No extra database table and no second dashboard: source, campaign and click ID are ordinary entry fields, so Fluent Forms’ own search, exports, reports and (with Fluent Forms Pro) Advanced Filter work on them, and they are kept, exported and erased with the entry.
  • One click per form. The settings screen lists your forms and the tracking fields each one still needs. “Add missing fields” appends them to the form as Hidden Fields through Fluent Forms’ own save, the same way the editor does; nothing else in the form changes.
  • A lead-source report inside Fluent Forms. Fluent Forms → Lead sources shows how many leads each channel (paid ads, organic search, social, AI assistants, email, other websites, direct), each source and medium, each campaign and each landing page brought, for the last 7, 30, 90 or 365 days, all time or any date range, for every form or one. It is counted from the entries themselves and shows totals only: no name, e-mail address or message appears on it.
  • Every lead gets a source, not only ad clicks. Without campaign parameters the source comes from the site that sent the visitor: search engines as “organic” (google, bing, duckduckgo…), AI assistants as “ai” (chatgpt, perplexity, gemini, copilot, claude…), social networks as “social” (facebook, instagram, linkedin…), any other site by its domain as “referral”, and a typed-in address as “(direct)” / “(none)”. Ad data always wins: an organic or direct visit never replaces the parameters or click ID of an ad. Only the referring domain is used, never the full address.
  • The landing page is recorded too, without its query string, so you see which page the lead first arrived on.
  • Meta (Facebook and Instagram) Ads work out of the box. Meta appends the UTM parameters you set on the ad — source, medium, campaign, content, term — to the landing URL, and the plugin stores them with the entry as they are, for example facebook / cpc / your campaign name / the ad ID. Nothing else to configure.
  • Survives the way people really convert. Visitors rarely send the form on the page they land on. UTM parameters are kept for the browser session; the Google Ads click ID is kept in a first-party cookie (90 days by default, adjustable), because it is only in the address of the very first page and people often come back days later.
  • Ad clicks without tracking templates. Auto-tagging adds only a click ID to an ad link, no UTM parameters, so most trackers record these leads with an empty source. This plugin recognises the click IDs of Google Ads (gclid, and gbraid / wbraid where Google sends those instead), Microsoft Advertising (msclkid), TikTok (ttclid) and LinkedIn (li_fat_id), and records the platform as source and medium: “google” / “cpc”, “bing” / “cpc”, “tiktok” / “paid_social”, “linkedin” / “paid_social”. A source the ad link does set always wins. For Google Ads the rule also runs on the server, just before Fluent Forms stores the entry, so it works even when the visitor’s browser blocks scripts.
  • Only what is needed is kept. Of the click IDs only the Google Ads gclid is stored with the entry (it is what Google Ads offline conversion imports use). The others are read once to name the platform; the plugin does not store them.
  • Fixes your older entries too. Entries saved before the plugin that carry a click ID but no source show “google” on the Entries screen straight away. A one-click, batched tool writes it into those entries for exports and reports as well, the way Fluent Forms itself stores an edited entry, and never overwrites an entry that already has a source or that someone edits in the meantime.
  • Last touch wins, campaigns never mix. A new campaign visit replaces the values of the previous one, so a Google Ads click after a Facebook visit is not recorded as Facebook, and a new source never travels with an old utm_content.
  • Consent-aware. With the WP Consent API plugin (used by Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot and others), nothing is stored until the visitor allows marketing cookies, and stored values are removed when consent is withdrawn. Suggested privacy-policy text is added to the WordPress Policy Guide.
  • Works with the free Fluent Forms. Hidden fields and entries are part of Fluent Forms itself; Fluent Forms Pro is not required.

Tracked fields

utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, gclid and landing_page. A field that is not on a form is simply not recorded, so you can leave out the ones you do not need.

Built to stay out of the way

The capture script is a few kilobytes, loads deferred in the footer, has no dependencies and does not watch the page: it fills the fields when the page loads, when Fluent Forms opens a form (popups, AJAX-loaded forms) and at the moment the form is sent. The plugin does not touch Fluent Forms’ Entries screen markup, so nothing shifts or breaks when Fluent Forms updates its interface.

Privacy

The plugin does not connect to any external service and sends nothing anywhere. The values stay in the visitor’s browser (sessionStorage and the qfut_gclid cookie) until a form is sent; after that they are part of the Fluent Forms entry and are kept, exported and erased with it. Of a referring page only its domain is used. Of the click IDs only gclid is kept; the others only name the platform. (Fluent Forms itself records the address of the page a form was sent from; that is Fluent Forms’ own data and is not changed by this plugin.) Recording organic, AI, social, referral and direct visits can be switched off in the settings. The report reads the entries Fluent Forms already stores and shows totals only.

Translations

The interface is translation-ready, and translations are delivered through translate.wordpress.org. The author prepares Hungarian, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese (Portugal), Italian, Russian, Turkish and Polish.

Trademarks

Fluent Forms, Google Ads, Gemini, Meta, Facebook, Instagram, Microsoft Advertising, Bing, Copilot, TikTok, LinkedIn, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude are trademarks of their respective owners. This plugin is an independent add-on and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by them.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Fluent Forms.
  2. Install and activate Qaiyo UTM Tracker for Fluent Forms (Plugins → Add New, or upload the ZIP).
  3. Open Fluent Forms → UTM Tracker and click “Add missing fields” next to each form you want to track.
  4. Open Fluent Forms → Lead sources to see the leads by channel, source, campaign and landing page.

That is all: new entries record their source from now on. If you prefer to add the fields yourself, the screen also lists the field names: add one Hidden Field (Advanced Fields → Hidden Field) per name in the Fluent Forms editor and type the name into its Name Attribute.
sections.faq:
Do I need Fluent Forms Pro?

No. The hidden fields and the entries are part of the free Fluent Forms plugin.

Why is utm_source empty for some Google Ads leads in my old entries?

Google Ads auto-tagging adds only a gclid to the link. The Entries screen already shows these entries as “google” / “cpc”; to have the value in exports and reports too, use Fluent Forms → UTM Tracker → Update older entries once.

Can I filter entries by source or campaign?

Yes. Fluent Forms’ search box finds any value across all entries. With Fluent Forms Pro, the Advanced Filter also works on the hidden fields (for example utm_source = google). The Advanced Filter reads the stored per-field data, so for older entries run Update older entries once; new entries are included automatically.

Is my form changed when I click “Add missing fields”?

Only by appending the missing tracking fields as Hidden Fields at the end. The form is saved through Fluent Forms’ own form service, so Fluent Forms checks and stores it exactly as when you press Save in the editor. If the form is open in the editor at the same time, reload the editor before you save it there, otherwise it saves its older copy without the new fields.

Which ad platforms are recognised without UTM parameters?

Google Ads (gclid, gbraid, wbraid), Microsoft Advertising (msclkid), TikTok (ttclid) and LinkedIn (li_fat_id). When the ad link carries one of these click IDs and no utm_source, the platform is recorded as source and medium. Under “Ad click detection” you choose the forms this applies to. With UTM parameters on the ad link you also get the campaign name, on every platform.

How do I track ChatGPT ads?

ChatGPT ads have no click ID, so they are tracked through UTM parameters like any tagged link: set them on the ad in the ad platform, for example utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=your-campaign. The plugin stores them with the entry and the report counts them under “Paid ads”. A visit from an ordinary ChatGPT answer (no ad) is recorded as “chatgpt” / “ai” when the browser sends the referring site; ChatGPT may also tag such links itself with utm_source=chatgpt.com, which is then stored as it is.

Why is a Facebook visit with fbclid not counted as an ad?

Meta adds fbclid to every link that leaves Facebook or Instagram, ads and ordinary posts alike, so it does not prove a paid click. The plugin uses it only to name the source (“facebook” / “social”) when the browser sent no referring site. For ads, the UTM parameters you set on the ad decide, as before.

Where is the report and who can see it?

Under Fluent Forms → Lead sources, for administrators. To open it to another role, return a different capability from the qfut_report_capability filter, for example:

add_filter( 'qfut_report_capability', function () { return 'fluentform_entries_viewer'; } );

The settings screen stays for administrators.

How does the report decide the channel?

From the medium first, as analytics tools do: cpc, ppc, paid… are “Paid ads”; “organic” is organic search; “social”, “ai”, “email” and “referral” their own channels; “(direct)” / “(none)” is “Direct”; any other tagged link is “Other campaigns”. Entries without any source are “Not recorded”: they were sent before tracking was set up, through a form without the hidden fields, or from a browser that blocked the script. Trashed and spam entries are not counted. Older Google Ads entries with a click ID but no source are counted as “google” / “cpc”, the same as on the Entries screen.

What do “(direct)”, “organic”, “ai”, “social” and “referral” mean?

They describe visits that did not come through a tagged ad link: “(direct)” / “(none)” is a typed-in address or a bookmark, “organic” a search engine result, “ai” an AI assistant such as ChatGPT or Perplexity, “social” a social network, and “referral” any other website (its domain becomes the source). They follow the usual Google Analytics conventions. You can switch this off under “Visits without campaign parameters”; then only visits with campaign parameters or a click ID are recorded.

An organic visit came after an ad click. Which one is recorded?

The ad. Organic, social, referral and direct visits never replace the parameters or the click ID of an ad; a new ad click does replace an older ad visit.

Can I get the campaign name for Google Ads leads as well?

Yes, by adding UTM parameters to your ads. In Google Ads, set a Final URL suffix (account, campaign or ad group level), for example: utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign={campaignid}&utm_content={adgroupid}&utm_term={keyword}. The gclid keeps working alongside it.

Where do the numbers in utm_content come from?

That is whatever your ad link puts there. Meta ads often use the ad ID ({{ad.id}}); use {{ad.name}} in the URL parameters of the ad if you prefer the ad’s name.

What if the visitor comes back through a different ad?

The newest campaign visit wins and replaces the previous values completely.

Can I record something other than “google” / “cpc”?

Yes, with the qfut_gclid_attribution filter, for example:

add_filter( 'qfut_gclid_attribution', function ( $values ) { $values['utm_source'] = 'google_ads'; return $values; } );

The other click IDs have the qfut_click_id_attribution filter, which can change their values, remove one, or add the click ID of another platform:

add_filter( 'qfut_click_id_attribution', function ( $ids ) { $ids['twclid'] = array( 'utm_source' => 'x', 'utm_medium' => 'paid_social' ); return $ids; } );

Does it slow down my site?

The front-end script is small, deferred, and does no work while the visitor browses; it only reads the address once and fills the form fields.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Everything happens in the visitor’s browser, so cached pages behave exactly like uncached ones.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: lead-source report under Fluent Forms → Lead sources: leads by channel, source and medium, campaign and landing page, by period and form.
  • New: ad clicks from Microsoft Advertising (msclkid), TikTok (ttclid) and LinkedIn (li_fat_id), and Google Ads clicks that carry gbraid or wbraid, are recognised without UTM parameters. Only gclid is stored; the other click IDs only name the platform.
  • New: visits from AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and others) are recorded as “ai”.
  • New: a Facebook or Instagram visit whose referring site the browser did not send is recognised through fbclid as “facebook” / “social”.
  • Improved: a Google Ads click without UTM parameters is recorded as “google” / “cpc” even on a form that has no gclid field.
  • New filters: qfut_click_id_attribution, qfut_report_capability.

1.1.0

  • New: “Add missing fields” adds the tracking fields to a form in one click, saved through Fluent Forms’ own form service.
  • New: visits without campaign parameters get a source from the referring site — organic search, social, referral — or “(direct)” / “(none)”. Ad data always takes precedence. Can be switched off.
  • New: the landing page (without its query string) is recorded in a landing_page field.
  • Suggested privacy-policy text updated for the landing page and the referring domain.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: See where every Fluent Forms lead came from: ad platform and campaign, organic, AI, social or direct. With a lead-source report.
